Bee Business - The Ethical Removal of Bees

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What does it take to ethically relocate a hive of African honey bees?

Unique Selling Point:
You have a honey bee hive on your property and would like them ethically relocated. You phone a Bee Removal company, but how sure are you that they know what they are doing? Do they effectively relocate the hive or does the entire colony simply die off because of Bad Bee Removal Practices? We team up with Nico Grobler of the Northern Beekeepers Association to see what some companies are doing wrong, and how it should be done.

Summary:
It's Summer and honey bees are out in full force to do what they do best - make honey. But often a colony of bees will create a hive in a place that is not suitable according to humans. The African Honey Bee is fairly aggressive, and with the rise in bee allergies, most people do not want a hive on their properties - especially in urban area. Since the African Honey Bee is indigenous to South Africa and threatened, it is advisable to remove the hive and ethically relocate the bees. The problem is that there are a lot of companies out there without the necessary know-how on how to remove bees, so they use the wrong methods and simply dump the removed hive on a plot somewhere. In this case the bees have almost 0% chance of survival. Nico Grobler will show us how to do it the right way. Removing hives at night when most of the bees are in fact in the hive, resting. They make sure they move the queen bee, her nursery apiary and as many of the bees as possible to ensure the survival of the entire hive.

Many Bee Removal Companies have a bad reputation. They charge R800 to remove bees, which they do in the day when much of the colony is out scouting for nectar. They often destroy the hive in the process, not taking care to protect the brood and the nursing apiaries. Hives are often just dumped on empty plots.

Further information:
We will call out an unethical bee removal company and film them undercover -- and then Nico Grobler will point out what they did wrong, and we will confront the company. We will how the ethical removal and relocation of bees.

The African bee "Apis mellifera Scutellata" is an aggressive bee with a hardy strain and capable of producing large crops of honey. Honeybees live in colonies ranging in size from a few hundred to many thousands of bees. The colony has three castes: one (mother) Queen Bee, thousands of (female) worker bees and a few hundred (male) drones. Every year, particularly around the spring season with the advent of the warmer weather, the colony begins to grow once again in size. As a natural part of their life cycle a breakaway new colony swarms off to start a new home some distance away from the original hive. So swarming is a natural part of the bees’ existence and unfortunately any cavity which is secure from the elements becomes a target home for the new swarm. Hence bees will colonies house roofs, meter boxes, pool motor covers, and drums, waste bins, bird logs, empty tree trunks and any other place they feel will make a warm secure home.

We cannot afford to eradicate our honeybee populations, whether they be managed colonies in beehives or feral colonies in the wild which are not managed by beekeepers. Bees provide one of the most important pollination vehicles for food security as well as being able to produce large amounts of excess natural honey when properly managed in beehives. Yet unfortunately bees are also very protective of their valuable commodities and the bee sting venom is one of the most potent venom of the animal kingdom. So when bees move into suburban, industrial or agrarian areas and become a nuisance to other people and animals they may need to be removed. Ideally a competent beekeeper is the right person to carry out this function because he understands bee behavior and our African and Cape bees can become very aggressive when their homes are disturbed. A person not trained in carrying out bee removals should never attempt to relocate a colony of bees. Bees, when aggressive and uncontrollable can kill humans and animals. The cost of spending a night or two in the intensive care unit of any hospital is not worth claiming the reputation of removing a swarm of bees if you have never done it before.

Beekeepers need to register with DAFF, but there are no norms and standards guiding the removal of honey bees. Therefore it is important to get someone who knows what they are doing. SABIO, the South African Bee Industry Association is a voluntary association operating in terms of its Constitution. Members of SABIO are subjected to certain norms and standards, but many Bee Removal Companies are not affiliated with SABIO.

Script:


Bee Business Script





LINK
The removal of bees in our urban areas is big business, especially in the summer months. In Johannesburg alone there is a long list of companies advertising the ethical removal and relocation of bees - often stating that they will NOT kill the bees…. But can they all be trusted?
v/o
SOME weeks ago, Joburg resident, Conrad Groenewald had an owl box with a beehive in his garden that he wanted removed.
Conrad Groenewald
I said to him I don’t want you guys to kill these bees and he ensured me no they won't.

Derek: Conrad, why did you select that company?

I actually did look on their website. It seemed very decent. They had a website with photos of how they did previous removals.
V/O
The next day a worker arrived at around 9am whilst Groenewald was out.
Conrad Groenewald
All he did apparently was to take out a long sprayer, spray the nest, pack up and went. That was it.

Derek: So what did you find here?

A lot of dead bees around here. Was all over my garden, my front door. Wherever we walked there was dead bees.
V/O
But this was not an isolated incident says beekeeper and specialist bee remover, Nico Grobler. In Gauteng alone there are quite a few companies who are not living up to their promises when it comes to bee removal and relocation.
Nico Grobler
Derek: What are some of the problems that you’ve seen with removal of bees?

I think the biggest thing is that people would very quickly come to a client and say “you can’t take these bees out. They are inaccessible.” And then they would kill them.
Nico Grobler
Derek: Nico, why is it so important to preserve as many bees as we can?

For me that’s a simple answer. I love coffee. Without bees I cannot have my coffee. 30% of all the foods that you and I eat are pollinated by bees and they recon up to 90% of plants worldwide are pollinated by bees.
V/O
Grobler is passionate about his bees and as a registered and accredited beekeeper, he explains that removing bees ethically is a time-consuming and specialist operation. To prove the point he invited me along to a bee removal at a house in Pretoria.
V/O
Tonight he is working with his 12-year old son, Darian who shares his passion for bees.

They take all the necessary precautions.
Nico Grobler
Derek: Why do you do this at night?
Well, if you and I can see, the bees can see as well. So in the day they’ll definitely attack us.
V/O
The bees have been living on top of the ceiling board next to the stoep.
Nico & Derek
Derek: Nico, time to suit up, hey?
V/O
Nico takes great care to make sure that an angry worker bee will not be able to find exposed skin!
Nico & Derek
Nico: Now I must just make sure that the collar and everything is inside the veil…
Derek: Ja, please check.
V/O
Grobler uses, what he calls the bee-vac, a specialist, GENTLE SUCTION DEVICE that DRAWS the bees into a gauze cage.
Nico Grobler
And it’s got airflow around all the sides of the cartridge and it’s to keep the bees ventilated at all times.
V/O
They start by opening the hive and vacuuming the frontline of worker bees. Then they carefully cut the combs out of the hive...
DEREK LINK
So far it’s been an absolutely professional operation. Absolutely clinical.
V/O
The combs are meticulously removed in order to preserve the structure of the hive.
Derek Upsound:
Another delivery Nico.

Thank you Sir...
V/o
Carefully the combs are cut and placed into frames that will eventually be placed in the wooden box hive.
Nico Grobler
Derek: Do you ever feel like you’re a surgeon?

What we often say to people “you should do this work as if you’re a surgeon and not a butcher. And unfortunately there are too many butchers out there.
V/O
A bee colony consists of female worker bees, male drones and a queen. Once the combs are successfully moved the remaining bees are vacuumed carefully. The queen is isolated and they’re all reunited with their combs in the new catch box.
Nico Grobler;
We’re going to smoke the bees from the cartridge down into the hive.
V/O
But this is not where Grobler’s work ends. The box hive, or catch box as he calls it, is now moved to his farm just outside Pretoria.
Nico Grobler
We put them in small catch boxes, or six frame hives, so we bring them here. And here we will literally nurse them until they’re strong enough to be put in a 10 frame box or a brood box as we call it.
LINK

Finding an ethical bee removal company that will effectively relocate your swarm of bees is tricky, but our experts advise that you look for a company with credible references, that is registered with the local Beekeeping Association and the Department of Agriculture - someone who will be held accountable by their peers...
Monique Beekmann
His workers came in, parked. Within minutes they wanted to leave again. They were done.
V/o
Monique Beekmann had a recent traumatic bee removal experience in Johannesburg with another, different bee removal company, called AA Bee Removals.
Monique Beekmann
We we really totally ignorant. And I really believe that people employ that company out of ignorance. Because they say and they also say on their bakkie, and on the corner where their business is based, which is just round the corner here, “help us save the bees” and it’s just devastating.
v/O
They removed the combs and put them in a bucket. They left the swarm behind and over the next 10 days the bees congregated on the side of her pool pump cover. After complaints another worker returned to collect the bees.
Video
It’s a process which happens in stages...
V/o
The worker explained that the bees were now going to be reunited with the combs but our experts are doubtful as the bees are needed to keep the temperature of the hive constant at about 34 degrees celsius.
Nico Grobler
The temperature no longer being regulated means that the honey would now melt out of the cells. The larvae in the cells are dead and starting to rot and literally ooze.
V/o
Having seen first-hand what it takes to remove bees ethically, we made a few phone calls. Of the three companies we phoned, one cancelled and one failed to arrive. However, two workers from the company, AA Bee Removals showed up late in the afternoon. We were joined by longtime registered beekeeper and removal expert, Rob Kryl on our stakeout.

The workers smoked the bees to subdue them, opened the cavity on the tree with an axe and reached into the tree and tore the honeycombs out. Within minutes they were done.
Upsound
Derek; How’s it going?

Worker: Okay and you?

Derek: Good thanks. So what have you done with the bees?

Worker: *points ot bakkie*

The workers refused to speak to us and simply ignored my questions. At the back of the bakkie was the remnants of this hive together with others removed that day.
Rob Krul
He cut and pulled out all the combs, placed them into a tub. There may have been three or four bees in the tub. And clearly when they had finished that operation all the bees were left behind.

Derek: There were some in the vehicle

There were some in the vehicle, but certainly no indication that there was a queen or anything there. My feeling here is that the swarm has been destroyed. There’s nothing to make of that.
Link
I have to say they’re acting like it’s a crime scene. All we want to know is the procedure they used and what they’re going to do with the bees and the combs, but not a word.
V/O
We spoke to the owner of AA Bee Removals Lauren Winchester, via Skype from the United States where she now lives.
Lauren Winchester
Derek: Lauren, in your opinion, what does an ethical bee removal entail?

Removing the queen and the combs safely. If she flies off she flies off. That means that all her workers will follow her. And that they have the ability to remain a wild swarm or being put in a box if we can. But the ability to conglomerate somewhere else and carry on as usual.

Derek: We’ve seen two very different operations. In the one case the combs are removed, the bees are suctioned, and they’re all taken away. With your operation the combs are removed and there were just a few bees buzzing around in the vehicle.

Ja, well. We do remove the bees. The bees do get put in a box, a little box that’s taken away… That particular hive you saw was a very small hive.

Derek: No I agree on that…

Actually that hive got rehived by my beekeeper as he got home.

Derek: We’ve got he pictures. There were very few bees removed. Very few.

Okay.

Ja I can’t say but for the most part we put a little box there. If they could find the queen they would have put the queen in the box. If they could have found the queen. In this case it was a very small opening. They couldn’t find the queen or she flew off…
V/o
In a written response, Winchester says no bees were killed in the process and the bees that were left would leave and join other hives.

We were also directed to a plot outside Johannesburg with a mountain of dumped bee combs that, an informant alleges, are regularly left here by AA Bee removals.
Lauren Winchester
We would never throw comb away. We keep the comb, we render the comb. We do beeswax and it is quite an important commodity. And we would never just throw… and we don’t go near Diepsloot!


V/O
Winchester also made it clear that she believes her business is under attack, stating that “much of the accusations against us are fueled by individuals with a stake in the industry and who stand to gain directly from an attack on our business.”...
Lauren Winchester
Derek, we’ve been doing this a very long time and repeat business for huge hospitals, universities, people that are very bee-aware. You know, I really doubt that if the bees were dying all over the place that this operation would have been going on this long.


Nico Grobler
Derek: What are the legalities here or does it just come down to ethics?

I think at the moment it mostly comes down to ethics, because there’s no real law at the moment that actually polices this - over and above the poison act, of course. And I think that’s the problem.




PROMO 1 11”
Bees are the world’s most important pollinators of food crops and great care should be taken when moving swarms from our urban spaces. What does it take to ethically move a colony?


PROMO 2 11”
Across the world honey bees are facing many threats and even so-called problem colonies should be ethically removed and relocated, but can all bee removal companies be trusted?


PROMO 3 11”
Honey bees are crucial in food production and should be looked after at all cost. But some of the very people who claim to protect bees, are doing the exact opposite...





*** END ***

Because they say and they also say on their bakkie, and on the corner where their business is based, which is just round the corner here, “help us save the bees” and it’s just devastating. v/O They removed the combs and put them in a bucket. They left the swarm behind and over the next 10 days the bees congregated on the side of her pool pump cover. After complaints another worker returned to collect the bees. Video It’s a process which happens in stages... V/o The worker explained that the bees were now going to be reunited with the combs but our experts are doubtful as the bees are needed to keep the temperature of the hive constant at about 34 degrees celsius. Nico Grobler The temperature no longer being regulated means that the honey would now melt out of the cells. The larvae in the cells are dead and starting to rot and literally ooze. V/o Having seen first-hand what it takes to remove bees ethically, we made a few phone calls. Of the three companies we phoned, one cancelled and one failed to arrive. However, two workers from the company, AA Bee Removals showed up late in the afternoon. We were joined by longtime registered beekeeper and removal expert, Rob Kryl on our stakeout. The workers smoked the bees to subdue them, opened the cavity on the tree with an axe and reached into the tree and tore the honeycombs out. Within minutes they were done. Upsound Derek; How’s it going? Worker: Okay and you? Derek: Good thanks. So what have you done with the bees? Worker: *points ot bakkie* The workers refused to speak to us and simply ignored my questions. At the back of the bakkie was the remnants of this hive together with others removed that day. Rob Krul He cut and pulled out all the combs, placed them into a tub. There may have been three or four bees in the tub. And clearly when they had finished that operation all the bees were left behind. Derek: There were some in the vehicle There were some in the vehicle, but certainly no indication that there was a queen or anything there. My feeling here is that the swarm has been destroyed. There’s nothing to make of that. Link I have to say they’re acting like it’s a crime scene. All we want to know is the procedure they used and what they’re going to do with the bees and the combs, but not a word. V/O We spoke to the owner of AA Bee Removals Lauren Winchester, via Skype from the United States where she now lives. Lauren Winchester Derek: Lauren, in your opinion, what does an ethical bee removal entail? Removing the queen and the combs safely. If she flies off she flies off. That means that all her workers will follow her. And that they have the ability to remain a wild swarm or being put in a box if we can. But the ability to conglomerate somewhere else and carry on as usual. Derek: We’ve seen two very different operations. In the one case the combs are removed, the bees are suctioned, and they’re all taken away. With your operation the combs are removed and there were just a few bees buzzing around in the vehicle. Ja, well. We do remove the bees. The bees do get put in a box, a little box that’s taken away… That particular hive you saw was a very small hive. Derek: No I agree on that… Actually that hive got rehived by my beekeeper as he got home. Derek: We’ve got he pictures. There were very few bees removed. Very few. Okay. Ja I can’t say but for the most part we put a little box there. If they could find the queen they would have put the queen in the box. If they could have found the queen. In this case it was a very small opening. They couldn’t find the queen or she flew off… V/o In a written response, Winchester says no bees were killed in the process and the bees that were left would leave and join other hives. We were also directed to a plot outside Johannesburg with a mountain of dumped bee combs that, an informant alleges, are regularly left here by AA Bee removals. Lauren Winchester We would never throw comb away. We keep the comb, we render the comb. We do beeswax and it is quite an important commodity. And we would never just throw… and we don’t go near Diepsloot! V/O Winchester also made it clear that she believes her business is under attack, stating that “much of the accusations against us are fueled by individuals with a stake in the industry and who stand to gain directly from an attack on our business.”... Lauren Winchester Derek, we’ve been doing this a very long time and repeat business for huge hospitals, universities, people that are very bee-aware. You know, I really doubt that if the bees were dying all over the place that this operation would have been going on this long. Nico Grobler Derek: What are the legalities here or does it just come down to ethics? I think at the moment it mostly comes down to ethics, because there’s no real law at the moment that actually polices this - over and above the poison act, of course. And I think that’s the problem. PROMO 1 11” Bees are the world’s most important pollinators of food crops and great care should be taken when moving swarms from our urban spaces. What does it take to ethically move a colony? PROMO 2 11” Across the world honey bees are facing many threats and even so-called problem colonies should be ethically removed and relocated, but can all bee removal companies be trusted? PROMO 3 11” Honey bees are crucial in food production and should be looked after at all cost. But some of the very people who claim to protect bees, are doing the exact opposite... *** END ***

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): What does it take to ethically relocate a hive of African honey bees?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: You have a honey bee hive on your property and would like them ethically relocated. You phone a Bee Removal company, but how sure are you that they know what they are doing? Do they effectively relocate the hive or does the entire colony simply die off because of Bad Bee Removal Practices? We team up with Nico Grobler of the Northern Beekeepers Association to see what some companies are doing wrong, and how it should be done.
metadata.Summary: It's Summer and honey bees are out in full force to do what they do best - make honey. But often a colony of bees will create a hive in a place that is not suitable according to humans. The African Honey Bee is fairly aggressive, and with the rise in bee allergies, most people do not want a hive on their properties - especially in urban area. Since the African Honey Bee is indigenous to South Africa and threatened, it is advisable to remove the hive and ethically relocate the bees. The problem is that there are a lot of companies out there without the necessary know-how on how to remove bees, so they use the wrong methods and simply dump the removed hive on a plot somewhere. In this case the bees have almost 0% chance of survival. Nico Grobler will show us how to do it the right way. Removing hives at night when most of the bees are in fact in the hive, resting. They make sure they move the queen bee, her nursery apiary and as many of the bees as possible to ensure the survival of the entire hive. Many Bee Removal Companies have a bad reputation. They charge R800 to remove bees, which they do in the day when much of the colony is out scouting for nectar. They often destroy the hive in the process, not taking care to protect the brood and the nursing apiaries. Hives are often just dumped on empty plots.
metadata.Further information: We will call out an unethical bee removal company and film them undercover -- and then Nico Grobler will point out what they did wrong, and we will confront the company. We will how the ethical removal and relocation of bees. The African bee "Apis mellifera Scutellata" is an aggressive bee with a hardy strain and capable of producing large crops of honey. Honeybees live in colonies ranging in size from a few hundred to many thousands of bees. The colony has three castes: one (mother) Queen Bee, thousands of (female) worker bees and a few hundred (male) drones. Every year, particularly around the spring season with the advent of the warmer weather, the colony begins to grow once again in size. As a natural part of their life cycle a breakaway new colony swarms off to start a new home some distance away from the original hive. So swarming is a natural part of the bees’ existence and unfortunately any cavity which is secure from the elements becomes a target home for the new swarm. Hence bees will colonies house roofs, meter boxes, pool motor covers, and drums, waste bins, bird logs, empty tree trunks and any other place they feel will make a warm secure home. We cannot afford to eradicate our honeybee populations, whether they be managed colonies in beehives or feral colonies in the wild which are not managed by beekeepers. Bees provide one of the most important pollination vehicles for food security as well as being able to produce large amounts of excess natural honey when properly managed in beehives. Yet unfortunately bees are also very protective of their valuable commodities and the bee sting venom is one of the most potent venom of the animal kingdom. So when bees move into suburban, industrial or agrarian areas and become a nuisance to other people and animals they may need to be removed. Ideally a competent beekeeper is the right person to carry out this function because he understands bee behavior and our African and Cape bees can become very aggressive when their homes are disturbed. A person not trained in carrying out bee removals should never attempt to relocate a colony of bees. Bees, when aggressive and uncontrollable can kill humans and animals. The cost of spending a night or two in the intensive care unit of any hospital is not worth claiming the reputation of removing a swarm of bees if you have never done it before. Beekeepers need to register with DAFF, but there are no norms and standards guiding the removal of honey bees. Therefore it is important to get someone who knows what they are doing. SABIO, the South African Bee Industry Association is a voluntary association operating in terms of its Constitution. Members of SABIO are subjected to certain norms and standards, but many Bee Removal Companies are not affiliated with SABIO.
